html:
A government campaign to modernise the villages of South Korea, launched by President Park Chung-hee in 1970. The name means New Village Movement.

The state handed out cement and steel to every village and let the villagers decide how to use it. Villages that did well got more. Thatched roofs were replaced with tile and metal, and villagers built roads, small bridges, wells and village halls. Electricity and new rice varieties followed. Farm incomes rose, and the gap with the cities narrowed for a time.

It was also a tool of control. The movement spread slogans of diligence, self-help and cooperation, and it helped Park's authoritarian rule reach into every village. After the June Democratic Struggle of 1987 it lost its political weight.

Along with projects like the Gyeongbu Expressway, it belongs to the fast growth of South Korea after the Korean War. Development agencies later promoted it as a model in parts of Africa and Asia.
sum: A government campaign to modernise the villages of South Korea, launched by President Park Chung-hee in 1970. The name means New Village Movement.
